item.text:
**No-go on the send as designed.** The definition-only candidate is worth designing, but the request audit and test still leave gaps that could make an apparent improvement misleading. The corrected census properly keeps the July disputed case apart; it remains evidence of a pattern, not proof of cause. [Census]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/CENSUS.md:57)

1. **The request has a fourth relevant occurrence.** The event instruction also says “when the topic’s wording names it, list it in `not_judged`.” Changing three places while leaving that sentence undefined risks two meanings in one request, particularly for the cap-on-approval case the arm is meant to protect. Audit it and all other occurrences against the exact candidate before freezing the request. [Current request]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/candidate-system.txt:13), [design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/DESIGN.md:19)

2. **The regression rule contradicts the stated treatment of disputed cases.** The five watch topics are described as “reported, not scored,” but Q/R/L failures on them enter the lead rule. L is precisely where the readings disagree. Keep their marks and disagreements visible, but define in advance which changes can veto the candidate and on what agreed basis; do not silently adopt one reading’s threshold. [Design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/DESIGN.md:46)

3. **The lead rule can miss harm on the motivating topics.** It checks Q and R only on the other topics. A candidate could improve L on its seven targets while making their questions or answer choices worse and still qualify as a lead. Read and report all marks on both arms, and include material regressions on the motivating topics in the decision rule. H also needs an explicit **cannot tell** outcome and controls for both rows of the table: the status of a settlement phrase or an allegedly already-judged distinction is not universally settled. [Design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/DESIGN.md:33)

4. **Do not silently shrink the test.** The rule is stated for seven motivating topics and 21 sends per arm, but the July requests may be left out. Fix the population before sending and refuse the run if its required requests cannot be rebuilt; otherwise return with a revised design and rule. Likewise, predefine incomplete calls and invalid or unresolved readings. [Design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/DESIGN.md:42)

5. **A low control count is not proof that the sampler failed to reproduce the defect.** With only three draws per topic, a control count of four and a changed count of one would satisfy the proposed ratio, but would be weak evidence. Size the decision rule against the topic-level variation and disclose what this small probe can resolve. Repeated sends of one topic are not independent matters.

6. **The budget needs enforcement, not only an average estimate.** Before a send, specify the full request/output allowance, reservation per call, concurrency, charges for missing usage and a stop that prevents the $0.50 ceiling being exceeded. Check the rebuilt control against the request production actually sends and prove that the candidate changes only the intended text. [Design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/DESIGN.md:76)

Arm B should remain only an idea for a later decision. Its example and any additional growth need their own audit; an inconclusive or harmful A result is not evidence that B should be sent.

I would welcome a revised design and its $0 harness checks for review. **Passing those checks should return to the council before the paid send**, so the exact population, request diff, control behavior and enforceable ceiling can be inspected.

CONSENSUS: no, because the candidate leaves a relevant request sentence unchanged and the decision rule can miss regressions or operate on an unspecified population.
